DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Although the Flowers Stay

STS-HS12-L3-13001400-HSELA1112-PTN-CFI-01 • HS English 11-12 • Varied Syntax for Cohesion and Clarity
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Real treaties are famous for their long sentences. Negotiators join the terms with words like whereas, although, and until, so that one side's promise and the other side's condition sit inside a single sentence that neither party can read apart. The two poster clubs in this print shop are doing the same thing with a design: one tradition carved the bold flowers, the other brushed the fine wave lines, and the sentence on the rail decides how both of them survive in one poster.
If you had to protect both traditions in one sentence, which joining word would you choose, and what would that word promise?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Ximena doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Ximena is doing and why that word holds two promises together, in two sentences. Use exact words, not "stuff."
2
What is Haruki holding?
Look at the picture. Explain what Haruki holds and its purpose, in two sentences. Name the item exactly.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what the teacher is doing and what it produces, in two sentences. Use an exact verb.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Explain what kind of workroom this is and your evidence, in two sentences. Name exact tools.
5
Tell me about the fusion wall.
Look at the picture. Explain what the fusion wall holds and how the two styles combine, in two sentences. Use exact nouns.
6
What is Amaia wearing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Amaia is wearing and what she is doing, in two sentences. Use exact words.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.W.11-12.1.c — Words, phrases, clauses, and varied syntax to create cohesion and clarify relationships. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
